title: Why Pago Florentino tastes the way it does

lede.text: One south-facing site beside natural lagoons, in Ciudad Real. The orientation and the lagoons give very ripe fruit aromas with a fresh feel in the mouth.

chapters.title: One site under a sierra
paras: The whole denomination is one site, by the humilladero (wayside shrine) called La Solana, in the municipality of Malagón in Ciudad Real.
The vineyard lies on the foothills of the Sierra de Malagón. The slopes face south. The natural lagoons of Nava Grande and Nava En medio lie beside the vineyard.

fly.label: Sierra de Malagón
fly.caption: The vineyard is on the foothills of the Sierra de Malagón, on south-facing slopes.

chapters.title: Sheltered sun, early harvest
paras: The slopes are sheltered from the north winds, so the site is a solana (a sun-facing slope). The orientation and the climate make Tempranillo particularly early here.
The grapes ripen sooner. The harvest starts 15 days before the surrounding vineyards.

chapters.title: A red built on Tempranillo
paras: Pago Florentino protects one wine type, a red made at least 90% from Tempranillo. Syrah and Petit Verdot can be blended in, but together they never pass 10%.

Each variety is made separately. Fermentation is started by the grapes' own yeasts under normal conditions, and the skins stay in contact with the wine for 7 to 21 days. Yields are capped at 10,000 kg of grapes per hectare, or 70 hl per hectare.
The wine is deep and lively. The nose is fresh and direct. In the mouth come balsamic, velvety sensations. It is rich and very expressive, with a long finish.
